title: Ameliorative Effect of Morinda Officinalis Oligosaccharides on LPS-Induced Acute Lung Injury.
authors: Qing, Cheng; Wu, Yanrong; Liu, Binbin; Wang, Cheng; Zeng, Zhenguo
one_liner_zh: 该文研究巴戟天寡糖对LPS诱导急性肺损伤的缓解作用，涉及分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a disease characterized by extensive lung damage and rampant inflammation, with a high mortality rate and no effective treatments available. Morinda officinalis oligosaccharides (MOOs), derived from the root of the traditional Chinese medicinal herb Morinda officinalis, known for its immune-boosting properties, presents a novel therapeutic possibility. To date, the impact of MOOs on ALI has not been explored. Our study aimed to investigate the potential protective effects of MOOs against ALI and to uncover the underlying mechanisms through an integrated approach of network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation. We discovered that MOOs significantly mitigated the pathological damage and decreased the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines in LPS-induced ALI in mice. Complementary in vitro studies further demonstrated that MOOs effectively attenuated the M1 polarization induced by LPS. Network pharmacology analysis identified HSP90AA1, HSP90AB1, and NF-kappaB as key overlapping targets within a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network. Furthermore, Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses elucidated the biological processes and signaling pathways implicated in MOOs' therapeutic action on ALI. Subsequently, molecular docking affirmed the binding of MOOs to the active sites of these identified targets. Corroborating these findings, our in vivo and in vitro experiments consistently demonstrated that MOOs significantly inhibited the LPS-induced upregulation of HSP90 and NF-kappaB. Collectively, these findings suggest that MOOs confer protection against ALI through a multi-target, multi-pathway mechanism, offering a promising new therapeutic strategy to mitigate this severe pulmonary condition.
abstract_zh: 急性肺损伤（ALI）是一种以广泛肺损伤和炎症失控为特征的疾病，死亡率高且目前无有效治疗方法。巴戟天寡糖（MOOs）源自传统中草药巴戟天的根部，以其增强免疫力的特性而闻名，为治疗提供了新的可能性。迄今为止，MOOs对ALI的影响尚未被探索。本研究旨在通过网络药理学、分子对接和实验验证的综合方法，探讨MOOs对ALI的潜在保护作用并揭示其潜在机制。我们发现，MOOs显著减轻了LPS诱导的ALI小鼠的病理损伤，并降低了促炎细胞因子的表达。补充的体外研究进一步表明，MOOs有效减弱了LPS诱导的M1极化。网络药理学分析确定了HSP90AA1、HSP90AB1和NF-kappaB为蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络中的关键重叠靶点。此外，基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）分析阐明了MOOs对ALI治疗作用所涉及的生物学过程和信号通路。随后，分子对接确认了MOOs与这些已识别靶点活性位点的结合。与这些发现一致，我们的体内和体外实验一致表明，MOOs显著抑制了LPS诱导的HSP90和NF-kappaB上调。综合来看，这些发现表明MOOs通过多靶点、多通路机制赋予对ALI的保护作用，为缓解这种严重肺部疾病提供了一种有前景的新治疗策略。
